title: Where does the point go when we divide by ten, a hundred or more?
description: A table of four numbers divided by ten, a hundred, a thousand and ten thousand is filled row by row. Each zero in the divisor moves the point one place left, and zeroes fill the gap in front. Keeko's doubt is that dividing by a hundred leaves the digits where they were.
teaching_notes: One idea: count the zeroes in the divisor and move the point that many places left, adding zeroes in front when needed. Watch for students who leave the digits unchanged or move the point the wrong way.

source: Complete the table: divide 21.1, 0.13, 214.6 and 58 by 10, 100, 1000 and 10000
video_script.why: A learner who has divided a decimal by ten sees one rule that works for a hundred, a thousand and ten thousand.
video_script.substitution: Each zero in the divisor moves the point one place to the left.
video_script.anchor: the table of four numbers and four divisors from the book
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks dividing thirteen hundredths by a hundred leaves the digits unchanged, so the number stays as it was.
video_script.payoff_line: The last cell is fifty eight divided by ten thousand, which is zero point zero zero five eight.

final_answer.spoken: the sixteen cells of the table, ending with zero point zero zero five eight

maths_rules: the number of zeroes in 10, 100, 1000, 10000 is 1, 2, 3, 4
video_script.design: The table stays on the board; each row fills as the point slides left, with zeroes dropping in at the front.
open_questions: The book's table prints 2.146 under divide by 100 and 0.0058 under divide by 10000 with the dividend cell blank; the worklist gives the dividends 214.6 and 58, which agree.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a table with four numbers down the side and four divisors across the top

marks.nums: the four numbers and four divisors appear in the table
marks.list: the four numbers are lit one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a table from your book about dividing decimals.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>We divide four numbers by ten, a hundred, a thousand and ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The numbers are twenty one point one and thirteen hundredths. The others are two hundred and fourteen point six, and fifty eight.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What numbers fill the table?

beats.on_screen: the table and its empty cells stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 10 has 1 zero, 100 has 2 zeroes, 1000 has 3 zeroes, 10000 has 4 zeroes; an arrow points left

marks.zeros: the zeroes of each divisor light up and are counted
marks.move: an arrow shows the point moving one place left for each zero

narration: <bookmark mark='zeros'/>Count the zeroes in the number we divide by. Ten has one zero, a hundred has two, a thousand has three, and ten thousand has four.
<bookmark mark='move'/>Each zero moves the point one place to the left.

marks.given: the four numbers and four divisors are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four numbers. Each is divided by ten, a hundred, a thousand and ten thousand.

beats.on_screen: To find: all 16 cells of the table

marks.find: the sixteen empty cells are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the sixteen answers and fill the table.

marks.s1a: 21.1 is written with the point marked
marks.s1b: the point moves one place left, giving 2.11
marks.s1c: then two, three and four places, with zeroes dropping in at the front

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, use the rule on twenty one point one. Move the point left by the number of zeroes.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Divided by ten, the point moves one place. We get two point one one.
<bookmark mark='s1c'/>By a hundred, zero point two one one. By a thousand, zero point zero two one one. By ten thousand, zero point zero zero two one one.

marks.s2a: 0.13 is written with zeroes ready in front
marks.s2b: the point moves left past the front, and zeroes fill the gap
marks.s2c: the last two cells of the row are written

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, the second number is thirteen hundredths. When the point runs out of digits, we add zeroes in front.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Divided by ten, zero point zero one three. By a hundred, zero point zero zero one three. By a thousand, zero point zero zero zero one three.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>By ten thousand, zero point zero zero zero zero one three.

marks.s3a: 214.6 is written with the point marked
marks.s3b: the point moves left one, two, three and four places
marks.s3c: the last cell of the row is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, use the same rule on two hundred and fourteen point six.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Divided by ten, twenty one point four six. By a hundred, two point one four six. By a thousand, zero point two one four six.
<bookmark mark='s3c'/>By ten thousand, zero point zero two one four six.

marks.s4a: a point is placed at the end of 58
marks.s4b: the point moves left one, two and three places
marks.s4c: four zeroes are counted for ten thousand

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, fifty eight is a counting number, so we place the point at its end.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Divided by ten, five point eight. By a hundred, zero point five eight. By a thousand, zero point zero five eight.
<bookmark mark='s4c'/>For ten thousand, count four zeroes and move the point four places.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the last cell 58 ÷ 10000 = 0.0058; the full table is complete
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The last cell is fifty eight divided by ten thousand, which is zero point zero zero five eight.
<bookmark mark='table'/>All sixteen cells of the table are filled.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the table
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 0.13 ÷ 100 = 0.13; the digits 1 and 3 have not moved; the bubble is crossed out; the zeroes drop in

marks.fix: the crossed-out bubble shows a hundredth must be smaller
marks.right: the point moves two places and zeroes fill the front

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks zero point one three divided by a hundred is still zero point one three. The digits do not move.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a hundredth of a number must be much smaller than the number.
<bookmark mark='right'/>The point moves two places left, and zeroes fill the gap in front. The answer is zero point zero zero one three.
